questions.question: Lakshmi Vishwanathan, who won the prestigious Natya Kalanidhi Award from the Music Academy was famous for which dance form?
questions.solution:
Lakshmi Vishwanathan was a legendary exponent of Bharatanatyam and a prominent dance scholar.
  • Honor: She was awarded the Nritya Kalanidhi by the Music Academy, Chennai, which is one of the highest honors for a dancer.
  • Contribution: She was known for her deep research into the Abhinaya (expressive) aspect of dance and her efforts to preserve the traditional 'Sadir' heritage.

questions.question: 'Natyashashtra', the earliest text dealing with performing arts (dances and music), was compiled by which sage?
questions.solution:
The Natyashastra is an ancient Indian treatise on the performing arts, encompassing theatre, dance, and music, compiled by Sage Bharata Muni.
  • Composition: It is believed to have been written between 200 BCE and 200 CE.
  • Significance: Often referred to as the 'Fifth Veda', it provides the foundation for the Rasa theory (aesthetic flavor) and the technicalities of Indian classical dance.

questions.question: Sangeet Natak Akademi, the apex body in the field of performing arts in the country, was set up in which year for the preservation and promotion of various forms of Indian music, dance and drama?
questions.solution:
The Sangeet Natak Akademi, India's national academy for music, dance, and drama, was established by a resolution of the Ministry of Education in 1953.
  • Inauguration: It was inaugurated by the first President of India, Dr. Rajendra Prasad.
  • Role: It serves as the apex body for the preservation and promotion of India's intangible cultural heritage.

questions.question: ‘Ustad Bismillah Khan Yuva Puraskar’ of the Sangeet Natak Akademi is NOT awarded in which of the following categories?
questions.solution:
The Ustad Bismillah Khan Yuva Puraskar is awarded to young artists (under 40) in the fields of Music, Dance, and Theatre, but not Literature.
  • Context: Literature awards in India are primarily handled by the Sahitya Akademi.
  • Objective: This award was introduced in 2006 to identify and encourage outstanding young talent in the performing arts.

questions.question: Padma Bhushan awardee Lalgudi Gopala Jayaraman was associated with which of the following musical genres?
questions.solution:
Lalgudi Gopala Jayaraman was a legendary Violin maestro and a towering figure in Carnatic Music.
  • Innovation: He is credited with evolving a unique style known as the 'Lalgudi Bani', which emphasized the vocal nuances of the violin.
  • Versatility: Apart from being a performer, he was a prolific composer of Varnams and Tillanas.

questions.question: Muthuswami Dikshitar was a great eminent singer, composer and poet of which music?
questions.solution:
Muthuswami Dikshitar (1775–1835) was a legendary composer and is one of the Trinity of Carnatic Music.
  • Style: His compositions are known for their slow tempo (Chowka kala) and technical brilliance.
  • Language: Unlike his contemporaries who wrote in Telugu, Dikshitar composed primarily in Sanskrit.

questions.question: Who among the following was the first music director to bring Rock 'n' Roll to Hindi tunes?
questions.solution:
Rahul Dev Burman (RD Burman), affectionately known as 'Pancham Da', is credited with revolutionizing Hindi film music by introducing Rock 'n' Roll, jazz, and disco influences.
  • Style: He blended global rhythms with Indian melodies, making him a favorite among the youth in the 1970s.
  • Instruments: He was famous for using unconventional objects to create percussion sounds.

questions.question: Which musical instrument is played by Yella Venkateswara Rao, an Indian classical musician and percussionist?
questions.solution:
Yella Venkateswara Rao is a world-renowned virtuoso of the Mridangam, the primary percussion instrument in Carnatic music.
  • Achievement: He holds a Guinness World Record for playing the Mridangam continuously for 36 hours.
  • Recognition: He has accompanied almost all the great maestros of the Carnatic tradition.

questions.question: Padmashree Mukund Nayak was honoured with the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award 2017 for which of the following categories?
questions.solution:
Mukund Nayak is an eminent artist from Jharkhand who received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for his contribution to Folk Music (specifically Nagpuri folk).
  • Specialty: He is a master of the Jhumar dance and song tradition.
  • Impact: He has been a key figure in promoting the tribal culture and folk arts of the Chota Nagpur plateau.

questions.question: Ramnad V. Raghavan was associated with which of the following musical instruments?
questions.solution:
Ramnad V. Raghavan was a distinguished master of the Mridangam.
  • Academic Role: He was highly influential in teaching Carnatic percussion in the United States, particularly at Wesleyan University.
  • Style: He was known for his elegant and crisp fingering techniques on the double-headed drum.

questions.question: Jagjit Singh was associated with which of the following fields of music?
questions.solution:
Jagjit Singh was the most successful Ghazal singer and composer of all time, often called the 'Ghazal King'.
  • Contribution: He is credited with making the Ghazal (a form of poetic song) accessible to the common man by using simpler language and modern arrangements.
  • Legacy: His voice remains synonymous with soulful melodies and meaningful poetry.

questions.question: Sikkil Mala Chandrasekhar is associated with which of the following musical instruments?
questions.solution:
Sikkil Mala Chandrasekhar is a world-class Flute (Bansuri) player in the Carnatic tradition.
  • Lineage: She belongs to the famous 'Sikkil Sisters' family and was trained by her mother Kunjumani and aunt Neela.
  • Technique: She is known for her Gayaki style, which mimics the human voice on the flute.

questions.question: Name the Indian sitar player who became a hippie music icon of the 1960s after collaborating with the Beatles.
questions.solution:
Pandit Ravi Shankar became a global cultural ambassador and a hippie icon in the 1960s after his collaboration with George Harrison of The Beatles.
  • Instrument: He was a master of the Sitar.
  • Impact: He famously performed at the Woodstock Festival and the Concert for Bangladesh, introducing Indian classical music to the Western world.

questions.question: Who was the first to introduce Brazilian bossa nova rhythm in Hindi film music?
questions.solution:
RD Burman was a pioneer who experimented with various global genres, including the Brazilian Bossa Nova rhythm.
  • Example: One of the most famous examples of this influence is the song 'Mareez-E-Ishq' or the subtle rhythms in movies like Aradhana and Yaadon Ki Baaraat.

questions.question: Bholanath Prasanna was associated with which of the following musical instruments?
questions.solution:
Bholanath Prasanna was a renowned maestro of the Flute (Bansuri) in the Hindustani classical tradition.
  • Legacy: He was the guru of the legendary flute player Pandit Hariprasad Chaurasia.
  • Contribution: He played a vital role in establishing the flute as a primary solo instrument in North Indian classical music.

questions.question: Zakir Hussain, a famous Tabla player, belonged to which of the following musical gharanas?
questions.solution:
Ustad Zakir Hussain, the legendary Tabla maestro, belongs to the Punjab Gharana.
  • Heritage: He is the son of Ustad Alla Rakha, who was also a pioneer of this gharana.
  • Technique: The Punjab Gharana is known for its intricate and complex Pakhawaj-influenced compositions played on the Tabla.

questions.question: Indian classical vocalist Rashid Khan belonged to which of the following gharanas of music?
questions.solution:
The late Ustad Rashid Khan was a stellar vocalist belonging to the Rampur-Sahaswan Gharana.
  • Style: He was known for his mastery of Khayal singing and the emotional depth of his Sargams.
  • Note: He was the great-grandson of the gharana's founder, Inayat Hussain Khan.

questions.question: Arnab Chakrabarty is associated with which of the following musical instruments?
questions.solution:
Arnab Chakrabarty is a highly acclaimed contemporary performer of the Sarod.
  • Style: He is known for his technically sophisticated and aesthetically pure approach to the instrument.
  • Instrument: The Sarod is a fretless string instrument used in Hindustani music, known for its bright, echoing sound.

questions.question: Which singer of Carnatic music was given the title of 'Bombay' by the people of Tamil Nadu?
questions.solution:
Bombay Jayashri (Jayashri Ramnath) is a celebrated Carnatic vocalist who was born in Kolkata but raised in Mumbai, which earned her the prefix 'Bombay'.
  • Achievement: She is a Padma Shri recipient and was nominated for an Academy Award (Oscar) for her song in the film Life of Pi.

questions.question: Dakshinamurthy Pillai was an Indian musician who used to play __________.
questions.solution:
Pudukkottai Dakshinamurthy Pillai was a legendary Indian classical percussionist who excelled in playing the Mridangam and the Kanjira.
  • Reputation: He is considered one of the greatest figures in the history of Carnatic percussion, known for his formidable technique and rhythm.

questions.question: Emani Sankara Sastry was one of the first Carnatic maestros to use a contact microphone to harness the full potential of which musical instrument?
questions.solution:
Emani Sankara Sastry was a legendary Veena player who revolutionized the instrument's sound.
  • Innovation: By using a contact microphone, he was able to amplify the subtle Gamaka (ornamentation) of the Veena, making it audible in large concert halls.
  • Position: He served as the Chief Producer of Music at All India Radio.

questions.question: Muthuswami Dikshitar belonged to which of the following music genres?
questions.solution:
Muthuswami Dikshitar is a legendary figure in Carnatic music. (This is a repeated topic highlighting his importance).
  • Contribution: He composed nearly 500 pieces, including the famous Navagraha Kritis (songs dedicated to the nine planets).

questions.question: The eponymous track 'Breathless' is one of the most notable works of which music artist, which was released in 1998?
questions.solution:
The song 'Breathless' is the signature work of Shankar Mahadevan, released in his debut album in 1998.
  • Feat: The song is unique because it appears to be sung in a single breath (though it was a clever studio construction) over a continuous stream of music.
  • Career: This track propelled him to stardom before he formed the famous trio Shankar-Ehsaan-Loy.

questions.question: Bhupinder Singh was awarded Sangeet Natak Akademi award in 2015 for which of the following musical traditions?
questions.solution:
Bhupinder Singh was a legendary singer and guitarist known for his deep, husky voice. He received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for Sugam Sangeet (Light Music).
  • Style: He excelled in Ghazals and playback singing, often collaborating with his wife Mitali Singh.
  • Instrument: He was also a proficient 12-string guitar player in Bollywood.

questions.question: Rattan Mohan Sharma is associated with which of the following musical gharanas?
questions.solution:
Rattan Mohan Sharma is an eminent classical vocalist belonging to the Mewati Gharana.
  • Lineage: He is the nephew and disciple of the legendary Pandit Jasraj.
  • Specialty: He is known for his mastery over Haveli Sangeet and devotional music, in addition to classical Khayal.
